source_title: Why HEIs should find a balance between teaching and research - The Hindu

Should colleges and universities try to do justice to teaching and conducting research and is such a compromise is feasible? | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockPhoto
O ne of the major challenges faced by higher education institutions (HEIs) globally is whether to focus on teaching or research. There are three core issues: Should colleges and universities try to do justice to teaching and conducting research, and is such a compromise feasible? Second, is engaging in research, especially high-end research, more prestigious than classroom teaching, which is usually talked about in terms of ‘load’? Third, do brilliant teachers automatically turn into exceptional researchers and, conversely, are outstanding researchers excellent teachers as well?
The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 talks about three types of institutions: Research-intensive universities, teaching-intensive universities, and autonomous degree-granting colleges. While all three should undertake teaching and pursue research, the quantum of teaching and how research is pursued and promoted differ widely across the spectrum of institutions. Affiliated and constituent colleges, especially those that offer only UG programmes, have modest aspirations. The faculty’s heavy workload, the lack of research infrastructure and ecosystem, and their commitment to shouldering multiple academic and administrative roles leave very little scope to conduct research. Autonomous colleges are better in terms of research; though the faculty have a heavy teaching load, they still undertake research, as projects, publications, and research guidance are mandatory for their upward mobility. Universities, on the contrary, have to conduct quality research, as it is their mandate to push the frontiers of knowledge and come up with new insights and theories.
Wilhelm von Humboldt (1767-1835), who established the University of Berlin in 1810 and is considered the founding spirit of the modern European university, envisaged universities as the ideal platform for advancing research. In fact, western HEIs, starting with The Johns Hopkins University in the U.S., are modelled on the Humboldtian paradigm of research-intensive universities. This does not imply that universities should shun teaching altogether. But in most western universities, teaching undergraduates is left largely to adjuncts and teaching assistants. In India too, in many universities, UG teaching has become the burden of doctoral students and the young faculty who are still finding their feet in the higher education stream. Senior professors should come forward to ignite young minds, identify and mentor bright minds, especially in terms of research.
It is a fact that, in India and in the West, conducting research is considered more prestigious and profitable compared to teaching, especially UG teaching. Whether it is recruitment, self-appraisal, or institutional assessment, or accreditation and ranking done by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) or the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF), research is a key component and crucial for boosting the institution’s grade and ranking. Globally, THE World University Rankings, QS World University Rankings, and the Academic Ranking of World Universities place significant emphasis on research alongside teaching.
While talking about the research-teaching nexus, excellence in one domain does not necessarily guarantee excellence in the other. Brilliant teachers are not always outstanding researchers and, conversely, highly competent researchers are not always smart teachers. Richard Feynman is a preeminent example of being an exceptional researcher as well as a teacher. Venki Ramakrishnan is another extraordinary scientist and brilliant communicator. But these are exceptions.
The frontiers of knowledge have to be constantly redefined and reconfigured, for the world is facing unprecedented challenges. New concepts, theories, and paradigms have to be generated and disseminated to address upcoming challenges. The trade-off between teaching and research in academia will persist, but the stakes increasingly favour research.
The writer is Emeritus Professor, Gandhigram Rural Institute, Gandhigram, Tamil Nadu

hi_body:
वैश्विक स्तर पर उच्च शिक्षा संस्थानों (HEIs) के सामने एक मुख्य चुनौती यह तय करना है कि वे कक्षा में शिक्षण पर ध्यान केंद्रित करें या शैक्षणिक अनुसंधान पर। इस विषय पर चर्चा आमतौर पर संस्थागत प्राथमिकताओं, प्रतिष्ठा और शिक्षकों की क्षमताओं के इर्द-गिर्द घूमती है।

## उच्च शिक्षा के मुख्य मुद्दे
- **संस्थागत फोकस:** क्या कॉलेज और विश्वविद्यालय शिक्षण और अनुसंधान दोनों को प्रभावी ढंग से संतुलित कर सकते हैं।
- **प्रतिष्ठा की धारणा:** अनुसंधान को अक्सर कक्षा में पढ़ाने की तुलना में अधिक प्रतिष्ठित माना जाता है, जिसे 'टीचिंग लोड' के रूप में देखा जाता है।
- **कौशल का मेल:** क्या उत्कृष्ट शिक्षक स्वाभाविक रूप से शानदार शोधकर्ता बनते हैं, और इसके विपरीत।

## भारतीय संदर्भ और नीतिगत ढांचा
राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति (NEP) 2020 जैसे ढांचों के अनुसार, संस्थानों को अनुसंधान-गहन विश्वविद्यालयों, शिक्षण-गहन विश्वविद्यालयों और स्वायत्त कॉलेजों में विभाजित किया गया है। हालांकि सभी शिक्षण और अनुसंधान करते हैं, लेकिन इनकी मात्रा और तौर-तरीके अलग होते हैं:
- संबद्ध स्नातक कॉलेजों में अक्सर शिक्षकों पर काम का भारी बोझ और सीमित अनुसंधान बुनियादी ढांचा होता है।
- स्वायत्त कॉलेज अनुसंधान को बढ़ावा देते हैं क्योंकि प्रकाशन और परियोजनाएं फैकल्टी की पदोन्नति से जुड़ी होती हैं।
- विश्वविद्यालयों को गुणवत्तापूर्ण अनुसंधान के माध्यम से ज्ञान की सीमाओं को आगे बढ़ाने का आदेश दिया गया है।

## ऐतिहासिक दृष्टिकोण और वैश्विक रैंकिंग
अनुसंधान-गहन विश्वविद्यालयों का मॉडल 19वीं शताब्दी में विल्हेम वॉन हंबोल्ट के शैक्षिक दर्शन से जुड़ा है। आधुनिक अभ्यास में, NAAC, NIRF, QS और THE जैसी वैश्विक और राष्ट्रीय रैंकिंग प्रणालियां संस्थागत ग्रेडिंग के लिए अनुसंधान पर महत्वपूर्ण जोर देती हैं।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन
विशेषज्ञों का कहना है कि शिक्षण में उत्कृष्टता स्वचालित रूप से अनुसंधान में उत्कृष्टता की गारंटी नहीं देती है, क्योंकि दोनों में उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शन करने वाले लोग विरले ही होते हैं। हितधारक यह समझने के लिए कि संस्थान इस संतुलन को कैसे संभालते हैं, आधिकारिक नीति दस्तावेजों और मान्यता रिपोर्टों की समीक्षा कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
Higher education institutions globally face a persistent challenge regarding how to balance the demands of classroom teaching and academic research. Discussions on this topic typically center on core institutional priorities, prestige, and faculty capabilities.

## Core Issues in Higher Education
- **Institutional Focus:** Whether colleges and universities can effectively balance both teaching and research.
- **Perception of Prestige:** Research is often viewed as more prestigious than classroom teaching, which is frequently described in terms of a 'teaching load'.
- **Skill Overlap:** The question of whether exceptional teachers naturally make brilliant researchers, and vice versa.

## The Indian Context and Policy Framework
Reported perspectives, including frameworks like the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, categorize institutions into research-intensive universities, teaching-intensive universities, and autonomous degree-granting colleges. While expectations vary across these categories:
- Affiliated undergraduate colleges often face heavy faculty workloads and limited research infrastructure.
- Autonomous colleges encourage research as publications and projects are linked to faculty career advancement.
- Universities are mandated to push the boundaries of knowledge through quality research.

## Historical Paradigms and Global Rankings
The model of research-intensive universities traces back to Wilhelm von Humboldt's educational philosophy established in the 19th century. In modern practice, global and national accreditation systems—such as NAAC, NIRF, QS, and THE rankings—place significant emphasis on research output for institutional grading.

## Practical Implications and Verification
Experts note that excellence in teaching does not automatically guarantee excellence in research, as exceptional individuals who excel in both are rare exceptions. Stakeholders and students can review institutional guidelines, accreditation reports, and official policy documents from bodies like the Ministry of Education to understand how individual HEIs manage this balance.
